sources.disposition_reason: The registered GitHub Well-Architected route automatically redirected to learn.github.com but returned no substantive page lines in either of two same-URL recovery opens. Identity, relevance, authorship, date, mechanism, and evidence posture could not be established within the authorized boundary.

The Claw-Eval repository home was used only to identify its current benchmark scope, human-verified task and rubric claims, Pass^3 policy, reproducibility caveat, and execution shape. Results and trustworthiness remain project-reported and unreproduced.
The official MCP introduction was used only to establish project identity, stated interface scope, and redirect correction. Its benefit and ecosystem statements remain project claims.

The scheduler continuum, commitment model, recovery protocol, and declared trade-offs were used to test whether execution topology should be a primary spine or a subordinate decision lens. The proposed Graph Harness has no completed empirical validation, and its 70-project survey substantially overlaps the same author's architecture study, so the two are not independent corroboration.

The Anthropic context-engineering article was used only to screen its coverage of context selection, tools, retrieval, compaction, notes, and subagents. Practitioner recommendations and observations remain source-reported.
The exact GitHub API identity endpoint returned an internal error and contributed no source content. The repository identity was instead pinned directly with git ls-remote.

The paper's constitutive test and neighboring-concept exclusions were used as a contested boundary instrument. Its conceptual analysis and six coding-harness applications do not establish effectiveness or authority over V2's broader interim boundary.
The Anthropic C-compiler account was used only as a first-party case study of loops, containers, Git coordination, tests, feedback, context-efficient output, parallel roles, and observed limits.
The AgentOps repository home was used only to identify a monitoring, replay, cost, evaluation, and integration implementation candidate. Its feature claims remain vendor self-description.

The registered everything-claude-code URL was used only to identify its automatic rename to ECC and expanded cross-harness operator-system scope. Project maturity, usage, and performance statements were not verified.

This first-party engineering retrospective was used only to test whether an environment-, feedback-, and failure-centered journey could organize later outline work. Its reported outcomes remain source-reported and coding-, organization-, and greenfield-specific; no claim or outline choice is promoted here.

The registered LangGraph endpoint returned only a redirect shell. No substantive content, identity metadata, mechanism, date, or evidence posture was inspectable without an unauthorized additional traversal.

This first-party practitioner article was used to test whether task shape and the workflow-versus-agent decision should precede mechanism coverage. Its customer and internal experience is useful framing but not controlled comparative proof or a pre-approved taxonomy.
The LangChain article was used only to identify a planner/executor split and its explicit lack of then-current benchmarking. It is vendor design rationale, not promoted effectiveness evidence.

The LLMLingua repository home was used only to identify a research implementation series for prompt and KV-cache compression and its associated source-reported results. This is narrower than general conversation compaction or durable context management.
The live MCP-tunnels page was used only to identify a product-specific private-network architecture, security model, shared responsibility, and explicit research-preview status.

The study's decision dimensions, recurring bundles, and explicit non-exhaustiveness were used to test a decision-centered organizing possibility. Its public-project sample and descriptive associations do not establish causal outcomes, field saturation, or a V2 taxonomy.

The live Claude Platform page was used only to identify current server-side compaction behavior, controls, accounting, and the visible beta header. Product documentation establishes vendor-described behavior, not comparative outcome quality.
The exact Live-SWE-agent v3 preprint was used only to identify its runtime tool-synthesis mechanism, experimental setup, reported results, ablations, and benchmark-specific evidence posture.

The Anthropic containment article was used only to screen its first-party account of approvals, sandboxes, VMs, filesystem and egress boundaries, tool-content trust, incidents, and product-specific telemetry.
The AWS sample repository home was used only to identify four runtime-specific human-approval patterns. It is sample implementation guidance, not comparative effectiveness evidence.
The ReAct abstract was used only to identify the interleaved reasoning/action mechanism, named evaluation settings, and limits of treating an older benchmark paper as general harness architecture.

The Letta repository home was used only to identify a stateful-agent implementation candidate and the material notice that the registered repository is a legacy server whose active development moved elsewhere.

The AgentBench repository home was used only to identify benchmark/evaluation scope, the 2025 shift to AgentBench FC, its current task packaging, and source-reported earlier benchmark results. It is not a CI-integration source.

The live Claude Platform page was used only to identify the documented tool-call/result contract, execution locations, schemas, choice controls, and product-specific scope. Documentation does not establish outcome quality.

The Letta article was used only to identify its agent-loop redesign, model-harness co-adaptation argument, transition rationale, and reported tradeoffs. Its primary subject is broader than the catalog's Memory & State placement, and its observations remain first-party.

The claude-devtools repository home was used only to identify a local debugging interface for transcripts, tool calls, token usage, subagent trees, and compaction. Its operation, privacy implications, and reliability were not assessed.

The natural-language/runtime/code ownership boundary and the paper's benchmark design were used to test representation as an implementation decision and auditability concern. Reported feasibility, mechanism metrics, and ablations remain specific to the paper's IHR, models, harness families, and benchmark conditions.

The unversioned LATS arXiv work page was used only to identify the reasoning/action/planning tree-search mechanism, named evaluation domains, reported results, and visible current version. The paper's claims remain experiment-specific and unreproduced.

The pinned AI Boost README was used as the complete catalog-enumeration input and for bounded repository-lineage metadata only. Catalog destinations were not opened, catalog categories were not adopted, and no evidence maturity was promoted.

The Dify root repository was used only to identify a broad LLM application, workflow, RAG, agent, and observability platform. The direct surface did not substantiate the catalog label Dify Human-in-the-Loop Node; resolving that specific feature requires a prohibited second hop.

The OpenAI long-horizon article was used only as a first-party single-run case study of durable project memory, milestones, verification, repair, and the Codex loop. The author explicitly distinguishes the experiment from production evidence.

The Anthropic engineering article was used only to identify its first-party experiments with planning, generator/evaluator separation, context strategy, sprint contracts, verification, cost, simplification, and model-dependent load-bearing components. Reported outcomes remain source-reported and unreproduced.

The Claude Agent SDK overview was used only to identify the documented agent loop, built-in tools, hooks, subagents, MCP, permissions, sessions, observability, and deployment surface. It is broad product/SDK documentation rather than specifically a generator or meta-harness.

The first-party Codex loop article was used only to calibrate direct relevance, mechanism scope, and vendor evidence posture. Its two catalog occurrences and repeated same-URL open remain one source family; no outcome claim or outline placement is promoted.

The DeepEval repository home was used only to identify an evaluation-framework candidate and its self-described agent, tool, planning, and MCP metrics. Metric validity and implementation quality remain unassessed.
The promptfoo repository home was used only to identify an evaluation, red-team, and CI implementation candidate. Project capability, adoption, privacy, and reliability statements were not verified.

The Mendral article was used only to identify its first-party argument for placing a multi-user harness outside the sandbox and its stated durability, credential, lifecycle, state, and filesystem-virtualization tradeoffs. The account is practitioner rationale, not independent security or performance evidence.

The LiteLLM repository home was used only to identify a provider SDK and AI gateway spanning routing, keys, spend, guardrails, logging, load balancing, and MCP/A2A. That scope is better described as gateway and production infrastructure than task running or orchestration.

The MCP servers repository home was used only to identify a steering-group-maintained collection of educational reference implementations. The README explicitly distinguishes it from the server registry and warns that examples are not production-ready.

The Phoenix repository home was used only to identify an AI-observability platform candidate covering tracing, evaluation, datasets, experiments, prompt management, and troubleshooting. All capability statements remain project self-description.

The OWASP page was retained narrowly for excessive-functionality, permission, autonomy, approval, and mediation controls. Prompt injection is one trigger/example, not the reason this source is relevant to harness engineering.
The OpenLLMetry repository home was used only to identify an OpenTelemetry-based observability candidate and a possible stale telemetry-policy contradiction requiring later resolution.

The TaskWeaver repository home was used only to identify its broad code-first agent-framework scope and the material fact that the owner archived the registered repository. Planning is one capability, not proof of the catalog's framing or of effectiveness.

The live Claude Platform page was used only to identify the documented self-hosted execution boundary, control-plane split, worker lifecycle, filesystem conventions, custom tools, and current product constraints. It does not establish general security or operational outcomes.

The OpenAI engineering article was used only to identify the first-party Codex harness and App Server architecture, thread/turn/item lifecycles, approval flow, persistence, protocol, client patterns, and integration tradeoffs. It is mechanism documentation, not comparative effectiveness evidence.

The OpenAI function-calling guide was used only to identify the documented tools, tool-call/result, schema, custom-tool, and tool-search surface. It is product/API documentation rather than the catalog's apparent educational collection.
The complete eleven-page seed was used only to map its source-native structure and anchoring hazards. It supports no promoted V2 claim or adopted taxonomy at this checkpoint.

The MCP project blog post was used only to identify its maintainer-authored risk vocabulary for tool annotations, trust limits, host-layer policy uses, composition risk, and open proposal questions. It is an official project argument and status account, not the specification or empirical validation.
